claims.claim: Visa reported 14% net revenue growth for the fiscal third quarter of 2026.
Net revenue was $11.6 billion, an increase of 14%.
Net revenue increased 13% on a constant-dollar basis.
GAAP net income was $5.6 billion.
GAAP earnings per share were $2.97.
Non-GAAP net income was $6.3 billion.
Non-GAAP earnings per share were $3.32.
GAAP operating expenses were $4.8 billion, a 19% increase over the prior year.
Non-GAAP operating expenses increased 17% over the prior year.
Total processed transactions for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were 71.7 billion, a 10% increase over the prior year.
Payments volume for the three months ended June 30, 2026 increased 10% over the prior year on a constant-dollar basis.
Total cross-border volume on a constant-dollar basis increased 13% over the prior year.
Cross-border volume excluding transactions within Europe increased 12% on a constant-dollar basis.
Data processing revenue for the quarter was $6.0 billion.
Service revenue for the quarter was $4.9 billion.
International transaction revenue for the quarter was $3.9 billion.
Other revenue for the quarter was $1.5 billion.
The release provides no guidance or outlook.
Cash, cash equivalents and investment securities were $13.9 billion at June 30, 2026.
During the three months ended June 30, 2026, Visa repurchased approximately 14.5 million shares of class A common stock for $4.9 billion.
The board of directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.670 per share of class A common stock on July 28, 2026.
Remaining authorized funds for share repurchases were $28.4 billion as of June 30, 2026.
The company recorded a $237 million litigation provision for the quarter.
claims.note: Release identifies $237 million as the MDL litigation provision special item excluded in the non-GAAP reconciliation; the GAAP litigation provision line for the quarter is $253 million, so the brief's phrasing is imprecise but the figure is stated in the release.

claims.claim: Visa deposited $250 million into its litigation escrow account on June 25, 2026.
Personnel expenses were cited as a primary driver of the 19% increase in GAAP operating expenses.
The exchange offer for class B-1 and class B-2 common stock settled on May 12, 2026.
